examples.ko: 우리 자리는 세 번째 객차에 있어요.
examples.en: Our seats are in the third passenger car.

examples.ko: 기차 맨 뒤 객차는 사람이 별로 없어요.
examples.en: The last car of the train doesn't have many people.
I almost fell while walking between the cars.

examples.ko: 객차마다 짐을 놓는 곳이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: Each car has its own place to put luggage.
This train has ten passenger cars.
I want to ride in a car near the restroom.

explain: 기차에서 사람이 타는 칸을 가리키고, 열차를 끄는 '기관차', 짐을 싣는 '화물차'와 짝으로 나와요. 실제로 안내할 때는 '3호차'처럼 말하는 일이 많아요. '세 번째 객차'처럼 순서를 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the cars of a train that carry people, and it pairs with '기관차' (locomotive) and '화물차' (freight car). When giving directions, people often say '3호차' (car 3). You can also say '세 번째 객차' (the third car) for position.

examples.en: The volume carried by rail has increased a lot this year.

examples.ko: 명절에는 택배 수송량은 평소의 두 배예요.
examples.en: During the holidays, parcel delivery volume is double the usual.
I'm worried because the port's shipping volume has dropped.
We need more trucks to increase the transport volume.
Compared with ships, planes carry less and cost more.
I looked up how much is transported per day.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 실어 나른 양을 숫자로 말할 때 써요. '화물 수송량', '여객 수송량'처럼 앞에 무엇을 나르는지 붙이는 경우가 많고, 뉴스와 경제 기사에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when talking about how much of people or goods was carried, in numbers. A word for what is carried often comes before it, as in '화물 수송량' (freight volume) and '여객 수송량' (passenger volume), and it shows up often in news and economic articles.

en: north of (a line or river); the northern part of Korea (North Korea area)

examples.en: My grandmother is someone who came down from the North.

examples.ko: 서울 이북 지역은 눈이 더 많이 와요.
examples.en: The area north of Seoul gets more snow.
North of the Han River, there are many old markets.
I heard a northern dialect from the North for the first time.
Naengmyeon is known as a food from the North.

examples.ko: 휴전선 이북은 일반인이 갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Ordinary people can't go north of the armistice line.

explain: '이북'은 어떤 기준선의 위쪽을 말해요. '한강 이북'처럼 쓰고, 아래쪽은 '이남'이에요. 그냥 '이북'이라고만 하면 분단 때 북쪽에 있던 지역을 가리키기도 해요. 지금 나라를 말할 때는 '북한'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 이북 means the area above a certain line, as in '한강 이북', and the area below is 이남. Used alone, it can also refer to the region that was in the north at the time of the division. For the country today, say 북한.

examples.en: I'm going to leave the highway at the next interchange.
There is a big rest area near the interchange.
I missed the interchange and had to go a long way around.

examples.ko: 새 인터체인지가 생겨서 시내까지 훨씬 가까워졌어요.
examples.en: A new interchange opened, so downtown is much closer now.
The sign says it is 2 kilometers to the interchange.
The interchange was so complicated that I took the wrong road.

explain: 고속도로에 들어가고 나가는 곳이에요. 순화어로 '나들목'이라고도 하고, 'IC'로 줄여 말해요. 요금을 내는 '톨게이트'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: This is the place where you enter or exit a highway. The substitute term '나들목' is also used, and it is often shortened to 'IC'. It is different from '톨게이트', which is where you pay the toll.

en: launch of a flight or ship route; start of service

examples.ko: 새 항공사의 제주 노선 취항이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: The new airline's launch of a Jeju route has been decided.

examples.ko: 이 배는 다음 달 첫 취항을 앞두고 있어요.
examples.en: This ship is about to make its first voyage next month.
They are holding a sale to mark the new route.

examples.ko: 취항 소식에 공항 주변이 들떠 있어요.
examples.en: The area around the airport is excited by the news of the new service.

examples.ko: 직항 노선의 취항이 늘어서 여행하기 편해졌어요.
examples.en: More direct routes have launched, so traveling has become easier.
On the first day of service, they even handed out souvenirs.

explain: 항공기나 여객선이 어떤 노선에 처음 다니기 시작하는 것을 말해서 뉴스에서 '신규 취항'으로 자주 써요. 계속 다니는 것을 말하는 '운항'과는 달라요. 비행기뿐 아니라 배에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a plane or ship starting service on a route, and appears in news as '신규 취항' (new service launch). It differs from '운항', which is about operating regularly. It can be used for ships as well as planes.
